payload.text: The amber light slants low across Greyhollow Ford, catching the river's spray and turning it the color of old brass. The ferry sits chained at its post, patient and useless. Ahead, the ferry-house door hangs open on one hinge, swaying slightly though there's no wind to speak of. Inside, the strongbox lies pried open and empty, a length of rope cut clean rather than frayed. Small tracks, clawed and close together, cross the dusty floor and lead back out toward the causeway stones. Overhead, the loft boards creak once, settling — or not settling. The bell that should have greeted them hangs still, its rope gone slack. The river roars on, indifferent, while the light keeps bleeding out of the sky.

payload.body: The ferry sits useless at its post, chained and waiting. Inside the ferry-house, the strongbox has been pried open and emptied. A length of rope was cut clean—not frayed—suggesting deliberate work. Small clawed tracks cross the dusty floor and lead toward the causeway stones. The bell hangs silent, its rope gone slack. The loft boards creak once, unsettling.

payload.text: Careful now — that board didn't creak for the wind. Goblins prize a good noise-maker as a ward against worse things; maybe that's why our bell went quiet. Peace first, swords after, I always say — or near enough.
I look up toward the loft and call out gently, telling whoever's hiding there we mean no harm and only want the bell ringing again.

payload.body: Tamsin Vale searched the ferry-house at Greyhollow Ford for signs of who cut the bell rope, but found no clues inside. The ferry remains still and the bell silent.

payload.text: I tell Wenna we will bring Pell home, and ask her for the safe path.

Wenna's head shakes once, eyes fixed past them on the causeway stones. The promise sits unanswered in the air between them.

Overhead, the loft creaks, and a shadow shifts quick against the beam — small, clawed, gone before it's seen clearly.
Kind words and a claw in the dark rarely mix, Odo.
Talk if you like — I'll keep an arrow on that beam while you do.

payload.body: We found Wenna at the ford, grief-struck over her missing son Pell. When we swore to bring him home, she would not answer—her eyes stayed fixed on the causeway stones as if she hadn't heard us at all. Above us in the loft, something small and clawed moved across a beam, too quick to identify.

payload.text:
The old posts guide Tamsin off the safe stones Wenna marked, out into reeds that close soft and whispering behind each step. One timber has gone dark, swallowed half under the current. Strung low between two reeds, a line of fish bones clatters faintly — a rattle meant to announce feet long before they arrive. Woodsmoke drifts thin on the air, sour with something scorched. Ahead, where the reeds thin toward higher ground, a shape crouches low and still against the failing light, watching the water rather than the shore. Kestrel's breath goes quiet at Tamsin's shoulder, bowstring already drawn half taut.

payload.text:
The arrow hisses past, close enough to part the hair above his ear, and buries itself in the mud behind him. Snag doesn't flinch — he's too busy sucking air through bared teeth, one hand clamped over the wound at his side, the other white-knuckled on the clapper-strap belted at his waist. Firelight catches the wet shine of blood between his fingers. Around him the other goblins' eyes dart to the reeds, to each other, waiting on him to break first. He doesn't. "Big-feet," he hisses, swaying but upright, "you want this bell quiet forever, you keep shooting."

payload.text:
Snag's back finds the clapper pole, and he hooks an arm around it, blade drifting toward the rope near Pell — close enough to see, not yet touching. His free hand jabs the air toward the dark water past the fire, then back to the leather strap at his own belt, the one worn smooth from years of guarding that same ring.

He sing-songs the offer into the night: the clapper stays, the river-things stay off his camp, and the big-feet walk out of the reeds whole.

The blade stays at the rope, waiting on an answer.

payload.text: Snag! You're holding that rope like a drowning man holds a rope - but you don't have to let go of everything to be heard. We've no quarrel with what guards your camp from river-things. Keep your ward if it eases you. Just let the bell ring once more before dark, and no blood need follow.
Kestrel's right that Snag won't yield easy - but a cornered thing bites harder than a bargained one. Let me try words while his blade's still just resting.

I lower my mace and speak directly to Snag, offering to let him keep whatever ward or charm he needs against the river so long as the bell rings free - trying to give him a way to back off without losing face.

payload.text:
Odo's mace dips, point to the mud, and his voice drops to something almost gentle. Snag's sing-song falters — the blade at Pell's rope trembles, then lifts away entirely. The goblin's free hand claws loose the leather strap from his own belt, baring pale skin beneath where it's never seen light, and he flings the strap toward Odo's boots rather than hand it over himself.

"Ward stays — big-feet keeps noise-thing," Snag spits, already backing from the pole. "River took my brother. Won't take Snag."

Pell scrambles free of the rope's reach, spear clutched tight, eyes on the goblin who just let him go.
